user.title: Connect to a TAK server
user.description: HA2TAK sends Cursor-on-Target (CoT) position reports for selected Home Assistant entities to a TAK server. TAK Server normally takes plain TCP on port 8087 and TLS on port 8089. With TLS you'll choose next between signing in with a username and password or using certificate files.

data_description.host: Hostname or IP address of the TAK server.
data_description.protocol: TAK Server silently drops data sent with the wrong protocol — TCP for port 8087, TLS for port 8089.

tls_method.title: How should Home Assistant authenticate?
tls_method.description: TLS connections to TAK Server need a client certificate.

menu_options.tls_enroll: Username and password (get a certificate from the server, like ATAK)
menu_options.tls_certificates: Certificate files (PEM or .p12 I already have)

tls_enroll.title: Sign in to {host}
tls_enroll.description: Home Assistant enrolls with the TAK server using your TAK account, exactly like ATAK's 'Enroll for client certificate'. The server issues a client certificate that is used for the TLS connection and renewed automatically before it expires. The username becomes the certificate's identity on the server.

data_description.password: When changing an existing connection, leave empty to keep the stored password.
data_description.enrollment_port: TAK Server's certificate enrollment API, normally 8446.
data_description.tls_verify: Turn off only if the enrollment port uses a self-signed certificate and you have no CA file for it. Your password is sent to this server.
data_description.tls_ca_file: Your TAK server's CA certificate. Leave empty to use the CA chain the server hands out at enrollment (or the system trust store).
data_description.tls_check_hostname: TAK server certificates are usually issued for an internal name, so hostname verification is off by default (like ATAK/iTAK).

tls_certificates.title: Client certificate files
tls_certificates.description: Paths are relative to the Home Assistant configuration folder (e.g. `ssl/tak_ca.pem`) unless absolute. Use either a PEM certificate and key, or a .p12 bundle.

data_description.tls_p12_file: A PKCS#12 bundle from TAK Server enrollment or a data package. TAK bundles often use the password 'atakatak'.
data_description.tls_ca_file: Your TAK server's CA certificate. Leave empty to use the CA chain the server hands out at enrollment (or the system trust store).
data_description.tls_check_hostname: TAK server certificates are usually issued for an internal name, so hostname verification is off by default (like ATAK/iTAK).

reauth_confirm.title: Sign in to {host} again
reauth_confirm.description: The TAK server rejected the stored username or password while renewing the client certificate. Enter the current credentials.

error.cannot_connect: Could not connect to the TAK server: {error}
error.cannot_connect_enrollment: Could not reach the TAK server's enrollment service: {error}
error.invalid_auth: The TAK server rejected the username or password.
error.invalid_certificate: The server certificate could not be verified: {error}

abort.already_configured: This TAK server is already configured.
abort.reauth_successful: Signed in again; a new client certificate was issued.

send_now.name: Send now
send_now.description: Immediately build and send CoT position reports for all configured entities to every configured TAK server, without waiting for the next reporting interval.
